liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Franklin's Tower** (4 reviews): Franklin's is described as slow, funky and syncopated; Jerry attacks the main lead break in Franklin's Tower with fire [10][11][12][19]
- **Help On The Way** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls the opening Help>Slipknot>Music Never Stopped run and They Love Each Other outstanding; Phil's strummed bass stands out on the Help>Slipknot opening [10][13][15]
- **Slipknot!** (2 reviews): Slipknot! runs a nice six minutes; Slipknot! did not lead into Franklin's because Jerry broke a string, says the attendee [11][17]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer finds this version oddly stiff, like a hotel lounge band; Audience-source DAT is missing They Love Each Other [7][14]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Reviewer finds Music Never Stopped a little lackluster but acceptable [19]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): The hot jam coming out of Truckin' shows the band still has it [14]
- **King Solomon's Marbles** (1 other source): Titled from the Blues For Allah CD sub-tracks, but tracked as a single song [2]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Jerry plays a standout lead about four minutes into Goin' Down The Road [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **King Solomon's Marbles**: rare: 6 archived performances [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1975-09-28.mtx.seamons.102155.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 15 songs; 112 min; rated 4.71/5 by 17 [1]
- **gd1975-09-28.fob.menke-falanga.motb-0069.91770.flac24**: source not stated; 15 songs; 112 min; rated 4.88/5 by 16 [2]
- **gd75-09-28.sbd.bertha-ashley.22257.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 97 min; rated 4.59/5 by 41 [4]. Said about its sound: Excellent, clear, bright, open mix; only Phil's bass is slightly weak [15]
- **gd75-09-28.sbd.fink.9392.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 97 min; rated 4.45/5 by 64 [5]. Said about its sound: Excellent sound; a harmonica player can be faintly heard on some songs, buried in the mix; Sound is strong and raw yet warm [11][18]
- **gd1975-09-28.aud.gofob.86250.flac16**: audience recording; 14 songs; 90 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [7]. Said about its sound: Slipknot has a minor digital glitch at its very end that could not be fixed [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says it was the only free park show in years, rumored for months [12]
- Jefferson Starship opened the day, and the Dead played Blues For Allah material [12]
- Attendee drove two hours from Sacramento and worked to the front as the band opened [17]
- Reviewer prefers this show to the 'One from the Vault' recording, their main 1975 reference [10]
- This show is often overshadowed by the Great American Music Hall and Winterland shows of 1975 [15]
- Setlist has no typical warm-up songs; the band is lucid from the start [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1975-09-28.mtx.seamons.102155.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN & FLAC>AIFF>Final Cut>WAV>FLAC16) [1]. Also: Matrix mix credited to Seamons, circulating as 16-bit FLAC [1]
- **gd1975-09-28.fob.menke-falanga.motb-0069.91770.flac24**: taped by Bob Menke and Louis Falanga; transferred by Bob Menke and Derek McCabe; source: 2 x Sony ECM-270 => Sony TC-152 >> MAC [2]. Also: Menke-Falanga FOB recording; various dropouts patched from soundboard and some patched to mono; Transition between Goin' Down The Road and One More Saturday Night is patched with soundboard [2]
- **gd75-09-28.sbd.bertha-ashley.22257.sbeok.shnf**: source: Sounboard [4]
- **gd75-09-28.sbd.fink.9392.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]
- **gd1975-09-28.aud.gofob.86250.flac16**: transferred by gotfob; source: On Stage Mic's (BY Band) > ? > Dat @ 44.1 [7]. Also: Left-channel dropouts on three tracks were patched using the right channel [7]
